name: turkish
title: Turkish
description: Turkish text tools: deasciify what was typed without the Turkish letters (Turkce yazilmis bir cumle → Türkçe yazılmış bir cümle, the pattern-table algorithm from Emacs turkish-mode), asciify the other way, and the Turkish cases where i and ı are two letters. Type, or select text in the app in front and open the palette; Enter pastes the row back, over the selection when that is where it came from.
author: pal

options.title: Paste into the app in front

store.tagline: Turkce → Türkçe, and the Turkish cases
features: Deasciify: ASCII-typed Turkish gets its letters back, decided by context (sik → sık, kus → kuş, acik → açık, yas → yaş): Deniz Yüret's Emacs turkish-mode table in Mustafa Emre Acer's JavaScript port
Asciify: the reverse, for a form or a system that takes no Turkish letters
UPPERCASE, lowercase and Title Case the Turkish way: i → İ, ı → I, and back; a suffix after an apostrophe stays down (İstanbul'da)
Type the text, or select it in the app in front and open the palette: the rows act on the selection and Enter pastes over it
Enter pastes (or copies, a setting), cmd+c copies, cmd+t hands the row to Translate, cmd+shift+c copies the source
Each row says how many characters it changed; a conversion that changes nothing is tagged unchanged
`pal://turkish/deasciify?text=…` (and asciify, upper, lower, title) for scripts; without `text` it converts the selection and pastes over it
